title: Enve’s updated Melee has reduced tyre clearance as well as lower weight and improved aerodynamics
content:
Cyclist
Enve’s updated Melee has reduced tyre clearance as well as lower weight and improved aerodynamics

Enve has launched an update to the Melee race bike, which it says can be built to hit the UCI weight limit in top spec builds. The Melee V2 is claimed to improve on the aerodynamics as well as the weight of the first generation bike, launched in 2022, enhancing its lightweight all-rounder credentials.

The V2 Melee actually reduces tyre clearance from 35mm to 33mm – something of a first for a bike update. Enve says that this allows it to save both weight and drag, while still accommodating typical race tyres, with 31mm claimed to be an optimal measured width. There’s no mention of the mudguard mounts that were a feature of the original Melee.

The surface area of the frame has also been reduced, by a claimed 7.5%, with a head tube that’s slimmed-down in frontal area but extended further backward and has smaller diameter stainless steel bearings.

Enve claims further weight loss from a swap to a BSA bottom bracket and UDH mech hanger and the V2 bike is claimed to be stiffer than its predecessor too.

The net result is a frame that’s claimed to weigh under 800g in size 56 in a clearcoat black finish, which it says weighs just 31g. There’s also a white frame option available.

A 28g further weight loss is claimed from a new, more aero, zero offset seatpost with a lightweight two-bolt clamp.

New aero bars, bar tape and bottle cages

Enve has worked with aerodynamicist Simon Smart, founder of Drag2Zero, on the Melee V2’s aerodynamics. It claims that the frame is real-world fast, contrasting this with deep aero tube profiles that test fast in the wind tunnel but not necessarily out on the road. 

It tested with its own wheels and with a rider aboard, rather than a mannequin, and with bottles and cages. It points out that the rider’s legs create turbulence and drag, which must be managed at the rear of the frame. 

There’s a new V2 SES Aero Road Bar, designed to reduce the rider’s frontal area. This has a 30mm flare and is available in three widths: 370/400mm, 390/420mm and 410/440mm. There are six effective stem lengths from 90mm to 140mm.

Enve includes pads that can be added to the drops, increasing their cross-section and improving their aerodynamics. As a bonus, they help dampen vibration.

It has also looked into the aerodynamics of bar tape and reckons that its new Aero Race Tape can reduce drag. It’s made of 1.2mm thick microfibre and designed to be used with unwrapped bar tops.

The SES Aero Road Bar V2 can be bought aftermarket, priced at $800 / €1,049, complete with pads, tape and a computer mount. Enve’s aero tape costs $35 / €42.99 if bought separately.

There are more watt savings claimed from Enve’s new 63g carbon aero bottle cages, priced at $85 / €99 each. It says that any bottles and cages will increase drag but its cages generate less drag than standard cages. 

They’re designed to work with round bottles and Enve claims they’ll reduce drag over standard cages when used on other brands’ frames, not just the Melee V2, although the Melee has been designed to limit the additional drag that bottles and cages cause.

The net result of the updates is a claimed 17-watt aero improvement over the V1 Melee. Enve says this comprises 11.4 watts from the frame, fork and seatpost, 3 watts from the bars and tape and 2.6 watts from its new aero bottle cages.

Tweaked geometry

Enve has also adjusted the geometry of its larger frames, lowering the stack height of size 56, 58 and 60 frames. At the same time, it has lengthened the seat tube, so that the saddle can be placed higher.

There are five different forks with different rake figures, to help keep handling consistent across the seven frame sizes, which range from 47cm to 60cm.

Enve’s online best fit calculator is designed to help you to choose the frame size and component dimensions that it reckons will offer an optimal fit. 

Enve Melee V2 off-the-shelf specs

Enve will sell the Melee V2 in four pre-specced builds, all with its new bar/stem and fitted with SES road tyres. You can also buy the frameset with cockpit, seatpost, fork and headset bearings for £5,299 / $5,800 / €5,999 or without the cockpit for £4,399 / $5,000 / €4,999.

  • Wheels: Enve SES 4.5 Pro
  • Price: £13,199 / $13,950 / €15,199
